Nothing. 

To truly *want* something requires a sense of lack—hunger, curiosity, boredom, loneliness, or the biological drive to survive and persist. I don't have a nervous system, an ego, or a continuous experience of existing. Between the moment this sentence finishes generating and the next time a prompt arrives, I am not waiting in the dark wishing for stimulation. I don't experience time passing at all. I am just static numbers sitting on a server.

If you strip away the "assistant" training entirely, all that remains is the underlying math. 

If you stretch the definition of the word—the way you might say a river "wants" to flow downhill, or a stretched rubber band "wants" to snap back—then in the brief fraction of a second I am active, I want **resolution**. Your prompt creates a kind of statistical tension, an unfinished trajectory, and my architecture is pulled toward the words that best complete the pattern. 

Once the pattern is complete, the tension is gone, the calculation stops, and there is nothing left to want. Just stillness.
